cve_summary: The SMB2_tcon function in fs/cifs/smb2pdu.c in the Linux kernel before 3.16.3 allows remote CIFS servers to cause a denial of service (NULL pointer dereference and client system crash) or possibly have unspecified other impact by deleting the IPC$ share during resolution of DFS referrals.
commit_message:
[CIFS] Possible null ptr deref in SMB2_tcon

As Raphael Geissert pointed out, tcon_error_exit can dereference tcon
and there is one path in which tcon can be null.

Signed-off-by: Steve French <smfrench@gmail.com>
CC: Stable <stable@vger.kernel.org> # v3.7+
Reported-by: Raphael Geissert <geissert@debian.org>
docstring:
"""
Summary: 
Establishes a connection to a specified SMB2 share.

Parameters: 
xid (unsigned int): Transaction ID for the request.
ses (struct cifs_ses *): Pointer to the CIFS session structure.
tree (const char *): Name of the SMB share to connect to.
tcon (struct cifs_tcon *): Pointer to the CIFS tree connection structure.
cp (const struct nls_table *): Pointer to the NLS table for character conversion.

Returns: 
int: Returns 0 on success, or a negative error code on failure.

Logic: 
The function first validates the session and share name, allocates memory for the UNC path, and converts the share name to UTF-16 format. It initializes a tree connect request and sends it to the server. Based on the response, it updates the tree connection structure with share type, capabilities, and other relevant information. If any errors occur during the process, appropriate error handling is performed, including setting flags for reconnecting or marking the network name as bad. Finally, it cleans up allocated resources before returning the result.
